transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-01
- Start time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Location: Zoom
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rohit Patel (Redwood SE), Jonas Vega (Redwood Solutions), Priya Rao (Argonaut Head of ML), Ethan Kwan (Argonaut Platform), Sara Lopez (Argonaut FinOps), Tom Berger (Argonaut Security)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage analytics, mapping traffic to cost buckets, and how to plan a pilot that measures latency vs cost for clinical-text-inference routes. Customer wants clarity on per-team chargeback and assurances on data residency + KMS.

Topics covered (approx):
- Landing page + dashboards (00:00–06:00)
- Per-route breakdown and attribution (06:00–18:00)
- Batching, KV cache, and cost levers (18:00–28:00)
- Security/compliance and private deployment notes (28:00–36:00)
- Pilot, benchmarks, pricing and next steps (36:00–48:00)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE for this region. I'll hand it to Rohit and Jonas to take you through the console.
[00:15] Priya Rao: Hi, Maya, thanks. We, um, are mainly interested in how we can tie inference spend back to clinical teams — our main ask is route-level visibility and chargeback.
[00:28] Rohit Patel: Totally, that's what we'll focus on. Quick agenda — show the usage home, then per-route dashboards, then cost breakdown and some knobs: batching, caching, quantization suggestions.
[00:40] Ethan Kwan: Side note, we have a requirement to keep PHI in region and keys in our HSM; we also need SAML SSO and audit logs.
[00:52] Jonas Vega: Yep, we'll cover private deployment options and KMS. For the hosted flow we also support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations, but we'll call out differences.
[01:05] Sara Lopez: And pricing — do you have example math for per-100k tokens per route? We need to show FinOps a model.
[01:14] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll send a worked example, and show the console telemetry that feeds the model.

[02:00] Rohit Patel: Opening the console — this is the usage home. Top-line trend, token volume, and a quick cost summary for the month. You can filter by model, region, and by route name.
[02:18] Priya Rao: Route name — is that from our app or do you generate it?
[02:24] Rohit Patel: We ingest route tags from your request metadata — you can map service names, team tags, or function ids. If not present, we fall back to endpoint id. Small caveat — sometimes SDKs don't forward tags so we have an enrichment step.
[02:40] Ethan Kwan: We'll definitely send sample headers.

[03:15] Rohit Patel: Jumping to per-route dashboard for clinical-text-infer. Top shows request count, tokens in/out, average latency, p95/p99, and cost attributed to the route. There's a toggle to switch between cost computed via actual host GPU runtime pricing or estimated list pricing.
[03:34] Priya Rao: How granular is the cost attribution? Can we see batch-level effects?
[03:41] Rohit Patel: We show per-minute aggregation and per-request breakdown if you enable payload-level telemetry. For batch effects we have a batching impact chart that models how your batching policy changed tokens-per-second and the resulting unit cost. It's modeled from sample kernel throughput profiles.
[04:05] Sara Lopez: Is the cost on the dashboard the final billable line item? Or is it a model for chargeback?
[04:12] Maya Chen: It's modeled cost for internal chargeback — final invoice might include margins or reserved capacity commitments. We show both: modeled per-route economics and the actual invoice reconciliation view.

[05:10] Rohit Patel: Showing tag-based split — you can group by team, product, or customer. Here I group by team, and you can see clinical team A vs B and their token splits and cost share.
[05:28] Ethan Kwan: Nice. Can you export CSV or integrate with our billing system?
[05:33] Rohit Patel: Yep, CSV export and webhook connectors to S3, BigQuery and some billing APIs. We can also push per-route cost signals into your internal metrics pipeline.

[06:05] Rohit Patel: Now the cost decomposition: token compute cost, NVidia spot vs dedicated capacity, and optimizer savings (cache hits, KV reuse). The console gives an attribution for each cost line.
[06:25] Jonas Vega: Worth calling out quantization recommendations here — for some routes that are low-latency tolerant we suggest 4-bit quantization to drop cost 20–40% with small quality checks.
[06:40] Priya Rao: We can't risk regression on clinical outputs... how do you guard for quality?
[06:46] Jonas Vega: We integrate with Redwood Optimize: you define evaluation prompts and reference outputs, and we run A/B comparisons on candidate quant/precision settings. We flag regressions and let you choose rollback thresholds.

[07:20] Tom Berger: On security: if we go Private (VPC) what's the control plane? Do you need egress to Redwood?
[07:30] Jonas Vega: Private deployment runs a customer-controlled plane; control plane calls are optional. For fully air-gapped, you'd run the whole stack on prem — we provide an installer package. For VPC-hosted private there's an outbound-optional model for license checks but logs and keys stay in your environment; with KMS we can integrate with your HSM.
[07:54] Tom Berger: Do you provide SOC2 artifacts and pen-test reports?
[07:59] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll share SOC2, ISO attestation, pen-test summary, and a security checklist. I'll drop links after this call.

[08:40] Rohit Patel: Scrolling to the route time-series — here's an example where batching was introduced on April 2nd, you can see tokens-per-second rise and per-token cost drop. But note p99 latency jumps slightly because of the micro-batching window.
[08:58] Priya Rao: That tradeoff is interesting. Our SLO is 200ms p95 for critical triage routes, but others can tolerate 800ms.
[09:08] Rohit Patel: Then we recommend a mixed policy: low-latency routes disabled batching + prefix caching; background routes enable 50–100ms batching windows and aggressive KV reuse.

[10:00] Rohit Patel: Demoing the routing policy UI — you can pin a route to a low-latency profile which keeps it on dedicated capacity or a hot-lane. You can also set a fallback to cheaper model variants automatically.
[10:16] Sara Lopez: How do you price dedicated vs hosted? Is it purely GPU-hours + tokens?
[10:22] Maya Chen: For Dedicated it's a committed monthly capacity — GPU-hour based with utilization tiers and overage. Hosted is per-token plus runtime compute. We'll include worked examples in the SOW.

[11:00] Ethan Kwan: For our pilot we want to run three representative routes: clinical-text-infer (critical), summary-batch (background), and semantic-search (medium). We'll need latency and cost numbers for all.
[11:14] Rohit Patel: Great — we can run those against your harness. The benchmark will measure cold-start, steady-state p50/p95/p99, and cost-per-1M tokens with different batching/quantization settings.

[12:05] Rohit Patel: Switching view to the 'Optimize' tab — this shows recommendations surfaced from production telemetry: suggested batch sizes, cache TTLs, quantization candidates, and predicted savings. You can accept a recommendation and stage it to a canary rollout.
[12:28] Priya Rao: Does canary routing affect billing while it's running? We need to show FinOps the delta.
[12:33] Rohit Patel: Canaries are tracked as separate routes in the console, with their own cost lines — you can roll up or exclude them from chargeback during evaluation.

[13:15] Jonas Vega: Also demoing the alerting — you can create alerts for cost anomalies (sudden surge), latency SLO breaches, and quality regression alerts from Optimize evals. We can integrate alerts into PagerDuty and Slack.
[13:30] Sara Lopez: Alerting for cost spikes is huge for us. We had an incident last quarter where a runaway job spiked token usage.
[13:39] Maya Chen: The anomaly detector can autosuggest a temporary throttle policy or redirect to a cheaper fallback model automatically.

[14:20] Tom Berger: For KMS we need to know whether keys ever leave our HSM.
[14:26] Jonas Vega: With our customer-managed keyflow, the key material never leaves your HSM; we use envelope encryption and only encrypted payloads transit the control plane. With on-prem it's all local. We'll send the integration diagram.

[15:05] Priya Rao: Ok, on governance — RBAC and SSO?
[15:12] Rohit Patel: We support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC per route and per-console action. You can lock down exports and billing sheets to FinOps role.

[16:00] Rohit Patel: Now a short walkthrough of the billing reconciliation view — you can map modeled costs to actual invoice lines and reconcile differences. This is useful for reserved capacity adjustments.
[16:20] Sara Lopez: Does the system account for spot preemption on GPU nodes?
[16:26] Jonas Vega: Yes — preemption losses are captured in the runtime telemetry and converted into an effective cost-per-token. We show adjustments and also recommend reserved capacity if volatility is high.

[17:10] Rohit Patel: Demoing the 'what-if' scenario builder — you can simulate swapping models, turning on a 4-bit quantized variant, or changing batching windows to preview cost and latency impacts.
[17:28] Priya Rao: Can that scenario be exported as a proposal for budgeting?
[17:33] Rohit Patel: Yes, there is a PDF export and a structured JSON export you can feed into your internal tools.

[18:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap — pilot with three routes, Redwood runs benchmarks, share SOC2 + KMS docs, FinOps gets modeled pricing sheet, and security reviews integration flow.
[18:12] Ethan Kwan: We'll send logs and a small sample billing export for you to ingest.
[18:18] Maya Chen: Perfect. Rohit, any other notes on the technical side?
[18:22] Rohit Patel: Just that we'll run a short smoke test first to validate tagging and telemetry ingestion, then the full benchmark. Expect initial numbers in 5 business days after we get the harness.

[18:35] Priya Rao: Timeline — we want pilot results 2 weeks after start. Is that feasible?
[18:40] Jonas Vega: Yes, assuming we get sample logs this week. The canonical plan: week 0 tagging/ingest, week 1 benchmark and A/B runs, week 2 refine and deliver results.

[19:05] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with the SOW and SSO/KMS docs. Also cc our support channel for the bench run.

[20:00] Sara Lopez: One last question — are there rate limits on the hosted API that could affect synthetic load tests?
[20:07] Maya Chen: For hosted we have rate limits per account; for benchmark we can provision test tokens or open temporary burst quotas. For Dedicated we can always provision more capacity for the test.

[20:30] Tom Berger: Security will want a joint threat-model session before production roll.
[20:35] Maya Chen: Noted — we can set that up.

[21:00] Priya Rao: Great — thanks team.
[21:05] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll send notes and next steps.

End of transcript.
